question: LASIK is suitable for correcting very high myopia (e.g., −15.00 D) in all patients, provided the pre-operative corneal thickness is greater than 500 µm.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. A cornea of 500 µm may still leave insufficient residual stromal bed after ablating for −15.00 D. The safety rule requires at least ~250 µm of residual stromal bed post-ablation; very high errors are better addressed by phakic IOL or refractive lens exchange.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Very high myopia requires deep ablation that can reduce residual stromal bed thickness below the safe minimum (~250 µm). In such cases, a phakic IOL or refractive lens exchange is preferred over corneal ablation, regardless of starting corneal thickness.
